title: How Japan Became a SUPERPOWER? | World's Greatest Comeback

segments.text: In 1945, after World War II, Japan was completely destroyed. Its cities were flattened, infrastructure ruined, and economy devastated.
Yet within just three decades, this island nation transformed into the second largest economy in the world. How did this economic miracle happen?
The first major pillar began around 1950 with industrial reconstruction. The Ministry of International Trade and Industry, known as MITI, coordinated industrial policy.

Following industrialization, Japan revolutionized its automobile and electronics industries. Companies like Toyota, Sony, and Honda introduced the kaizen philosophy of continuous improvement and zero defects.
Between 1960 and 1980, Japanese exports surged worldwide. High quality transistor radios, fuel-efficient automobiles, and consumer electronics dominated international markets.
Another crucial factor was massive investment in public education and high-speed infrastructure, such as the famous Shinkansen bullet train launched in 1964.
However, by the late 1980s, an asset price bubble formed in real estate and stocks, leading to the economic stagnation known as the Lost Decades.
In conclusion, Japan's post-war rise remains one of history's greatest economic turnarounds, driven by disciplined industrial planning, technological innovation, and relentless manufacturing quality.
